accessNotes: CORRECTION TO PRIOR ASSUMPTION: FTMO DOES publish per-tier pricing on stable public URLs. The pricing table is a client-side React widget (#pricing anchor) so prices do NOT appear in WebFetch's rendered-markdown output, which is almost certainly why earlier passes concluded 'no per-tier pricing on a stable URL'. However, the full price list is served in the initial HTML of every page carrying the widget, as a JSON blob in an inline <script id="pricing-table-data-js-extra"> assigning var ftmoPricingTable. Verified identical price arrays on three independent stable URLs: https://ftmo.com/en/ , https://ftmo.com/en/2-step-challenge/ , https://ftmo.com/en/1-step-challenge/ . No geo-block, no auth wall, no JS execution required to read the numbers (HTTP 200, plain curl with a browser UA). The widget renders prices from prices.step_2[i] / prices.step_1[i], indexed positionally against items[currency].challenges[i]; for currency USD the balances are, in order, 200000, 100000, 50000, 25000, 10000 -- so the price arrays map to account sizes largest-to-smallest. Independent confirmation of that positional mapping comes from the promo tooltip on index 1, which names the account size explicitly. Client-side rendering logic in https://ftmo.com/app/themes/ftmo-com/build/js/pricing-table-v2-TqeInASd.js is formattedPrice: N(o?"USD":"EUR", price) where o = onlyUsdCurrency; every ftmo.com locale checked ships "only_usd_currency":false, so the displayed fee is EUR-formatted. NOT VERIFIED: whether a US visitor is redirected to a separate USD-priced entity. ftmo.com/en/ declares <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://ftmo.oanda.com/"> and an in-page region switcher offering 'United States' -> https://ftmo.oanda.com/ . That is a DIFFERENT DOMAIN (FTMO/OANDA US joint entity) and was deliberately NOT scraped, per the rule that figures must come from ftmo.com itself. US-market pricing is therefore uncaptured and may differ entirely.
currencyNote: ALL CAPTURED PRICES ARE EUR, NOT USD. priceUsd is null for every tier because ftmo.com does not publish a USD fee anywhere -- no conversion was performed. Note the split denomination: ACCOUNT SIZES are selectable per currency (USD/GBP/EUR/CZK/CAD/AUD/CHF) and the USD ladder is 200k/100k/50k/25k/10k, but the FEE is one shared number rendered with a EUR symbol. Proof they are denominated separately, verbatim from the promo tooltip on the $100,000 tier: "Special Deal! $100,000 FTMO Challenge for €439 – only if you don't already have one active." -- dollar-denominated account, euro-denominated fee, on the same tier. So a trader buying the $100,000 USD 2-Step account is charged EUR 540 (list). sizeUsd values below are genuine USD account balances; priceEur values are genuine EUR fees; the two are simply quoted in different currencies by FTMO itself.

rules.news: No restriction during the Evaluation Process. On a funded FTMO Account, Standard account type only: no opening/closing trades (incl. SL/TP) from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after selected news releases. Swing account type: no news restriction.
rules.weekend: No restriction during Evaluation. On FTMO Account, weekend-holding restriction applies to Standard account type only; Swing has no restriction.
rules.overnight: No restriction during Evaluation. On FTMO Account, overnight-holding restriction applies to Standard account type only; Swing has no restriction.
rules.ea: Allowed. Expert Advisors permitted subject to legitimate trading and platform limits of 200 orders at a time and 2000 max positions per day. Third-party EAs carry max-capital-allocation risk.

fieldEvidence.maxLossPct: "The Maximum Loss Limit is a balance-based end-of-day trailing limit. The Max Loss Amount is 10% of initial balance (Initial Simulated Capital)."
fieldEvidence.drawdownType: "Maximum Loss Limit is a balance-based end-of-day trailing limit. It is calculated at the end of a trading day and sets a limit the account equity cannot reach or fall beneath." ... it "can only increase, but never decrease", and resets "when a Reward is withdrawn". This is the key structural difference from the 2-Step, whose max loss is static.

fieldEvidence.maxTradingDays: No limit published. "trading_period" steps: {"step_1":"Unlimited","step_3":"Unlimited"}. Recorded as null.
fieldEvidence.consistencyRulePct: "Best Day Rule" = 50%. Verbatim: "Your most profitable trading day (“Best Day”) must not account for more than 50% of your Positive Days' Profit." and "Best Day does not represent more than 50% of your Positive Days' Profit". Detail: "The Best Day is a single day with the highest profit from closed trades, calculated at the end of the trading day (00:00 CE(S)T), or when the other Trading Objectives are fulfilled. If the profit from your Best Day exceeds this 50% threshold, you must continue and earn additional profit until no single day represents more than half of the Positive Days' Profit in order to pass the FTMO Challenge or withdraw a Reward." Applies to both the challenge and to reward withdrawal.
fieldEvidence.profitSplitPct: "FTMO Challenge: 1-Step: You receive 90% of the profit. Rewards cannot be left on the account to grow the balance." and "90% of your simulated profits".

fieldEvidence.payoutFrequency: on-demand after day 14, same mechanism as 2-Step.
